clue.text: Agitated that chick endlessly with small talk

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up, so the fodder is rearranged
endlessly says the word chick loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone flustered by a chick passes the time in idle conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CHICK to CHIC; 'Agitated' then rearranges THAT plus CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, inconsequential conversation is chatter, idle gossip of the same kind.

clue.text: Support armed robbery

explanation.surface: A backer of a gun-wielding raid on a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up is to bear its weight, and a hold-up is also a stick-up by robbers with weapons.

clue.text: To eleven hundred it is poisonous

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A dose at eleven hundred hours proves deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic substance is a harmful, venomous one, a direct synonym.

clue.text: There's something afoot in the stable

definitions.text: There's something afoot in the stable

parts.words: There's something afoot in the stable
parts.note: afoot reads literally: an item fixed on the foot of a horse kept in a stable

explanation.surface: Something suspicious is going on among the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved iron plate nailed to a horse's hoof is literally on a foot in the stable.

clue.text: Man uprooted tree outside small enclosure

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters sit around the other piece
a tree uprooted is disturbed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: enc. is the short form of enclosure in letters

explanation.surface: A fellow has dug up a tree around a little pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprooted' turns TREE into TERE; 'outside' puts that around ENC, the abbreviation of enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence is a male first name, so it stands for a particular man.

clue.text: Some pressure put enthusiastically on fame

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A celebrity is keen to push their image hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'on fame' as the definition; 'on' is only a link, and 'fame' alone substitutes for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown and reputation are both the standing a person has in public estimation.

clue.text: Bishop keeps welcome for lively person

indicators.note: keeps means the bishop holds the greeting inside

parts.note: a bishop is styled Right Reverend, abbreviated RR
ave is a Latin word of greeting

explanation.surface: A clergyman gives a warm greeting to an energetic guest.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend, a bishop's title) holds AVE, Latin for hail.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who parties wildly, an exuberant type.

clue.text: One play is re-enacted in the islands

indicators.note: a play re-enacted is staged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single drama is staged again somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is a large group of Pacific island chains.

clue.text: Abstinent oriental with young child feeds the duck

indicators.note: feeds means these pieces go into the bird

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A teetotal man from the east and a toddler give bread to a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeds' puts E plus TOT inside TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses all alcohol is abstinent, a non-drinker.

clue.text: Priest, about nine, had recipe for sovereign remedy

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: about means the numeral is turned round

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A clergyman around nine o'clock had a formula for a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IX to XI; R comes from the Latin recipe heading old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed cure-all, a panacea for every ill.

clue.text: Top gun

explanation.surface: The best shot in the squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is something that turns around, and a pistol with a rotating cylinder is a handgun.

clue.text: Meat served at meal during the day?

definitions.text: Meat served at meal during the day?

parts.words: Meat served at meal during the day?
parts.note: describes both a tinned processed meat and the formal midday meal at which it might be served

explanation.surface: What sort of meat is served at a daytime meal?
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tinned pork product and a formal midday meal.

clue.text: Haphazard money order

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Instructions to pay are given out without any system.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard happens by chance, without plan or method.

clue.text: Fast start

parts.note: fast means a period of abstinence, and this day begins the Christian fast of Lent

explanation.surface: Get off the mark quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The first day of Lent opens forty days of religious abstinence.

clue.text: Highflier prepared a nut roast

indicators.note: a dish prepared is made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vegetarian dish is cooked for a high achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller flies higher than anyone, so is literally a high flier.

clue.text: As much as a sewer will hold?

definitions.text: As much as a sewer will hold?

parts.words: As much as a sewer will hold?
parts.note: sewer here means one who sews, not a drain; the quantity is the thread on a stitching tool

explanation.surface: What is the capacity of a drain?
explanation.definitionFit: A length of thread threaded at one time is the amount a stitcher works with.

clue.text: Turn pale with quip about ornamental work

indicators.note: turn means the words are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes white after a witty remark about their decorative stitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Applique is decoration made by sewing cut pieces of fabric onto a base.

clue.text: Saw a hen moving round yard, a carnivore

parts.note: saw in the sense of noticed

indicators.note: round means they sit about the yard's letter
moving means the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer watched a hen wandering about the yard, then a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges A HEN to HENA; 'round' puts it about Y.
explanation.definitionFit: This African scavenger is a meat-eating mammal.

clue.text: A heron's fluttering round English resort

indicators.note: the bird's fluttering about scrambles its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A heron flaps about over a seaside town in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornsea is a seaside town on the Yorkshire coast of England.

clue.text: Cage about to be brought up to woodworker

parts.note: a coop is a cage for poultry

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means reading upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cage is lifted up to the carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'brought up' turns RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooper is a craftsman who makes barrels and casks from timber.

clue.text: Nearly, nearly everybody, nearly everybody

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everybody stops short of its final letter

parts.note: all means everybody
most means nearly everybody

explanation.surface: A repetitive stammer about almost the whole crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ALL to AL; the second 'nearly everybody' gives MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly both mean not quite, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Thanks one going to Georgia forest

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
I is the Roman numeral one
GA is the US state code for Georgia

explanation.surface: Grateful, someone heads to Georgia's woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the coniferous woodland belt of the subarctic.

clue.text: Volume of regulations used by monarch?

definitions.text: Volume of regulations used by monarch?

parts.words: Volume of regulations used by monarch?
parts.note: a book of regulations, playfully imagined as a ruler's own book

explanation.surface: What does a king consult to govern?
explanation.definitionFit: A compendium of regulations is a manual of the laws of a game or body.

clue.text: Monk has no hesitation producing soup

indicators.note: has no means the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: a monk is a brother in a religious order
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A monk confidently serves a bowl of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin soup made from stock.

clue.text: Sign of water by one in western half of Russia

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the letters from Russia
western half of means the first half of Russia's letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A star sign suggests water in the western part of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western half of' takes RUS from Russia, and I sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius, the water carrier, is one of the twelve zodiac signs.

clue.text: Disc tending to be a failure?

explanation.surface: A record that is likely to flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy is a flexible computer diskette, and floppy also means inclined to droop or flop.

clue.text: Mooring a lady

parts.note: a berth is a ship's mooring place

explanation.surface: A woman ties up her boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's name, so it stands for a particular lady.

clue.text: Nothing here is completely sane?

parts.note: if nothing is here, everything must be elsewhere; the phrase also means fully rational

explanation.surface: Is everyone in this place a little mad?
explanation.definitionFit: To be mentally sharp and rational is idiomatically to have all one's faculties present.
